title: Onboarding Hub: a day-one checklist grounded in your own docs
description: A guided first-week hub for new hires: a checklist with progress, and every step able to answer itself from your own onboarding content.
prerequisites: A Glean instance with your onboarding content indexed
For the Platform Chat path: a token with the CHAT scope, plus X_GLEAN_INCLUDE_EXPERIMENTAL=true
For the Web SDK path: nothing beyond SSO — the browser session carries the identity
Node 20+ for the Platform path, or any static page for the Web SDK path

demoQueries.query: What should I do on my first day?
demoQueries.expectedBehavior: Returns a cited answer drawn from your own onboarding documents, and the checklist reflects steps that actually appear in them rather than a hardcoded list.

demoQueries.query: How do I set up VPN?
demoQueries.expectedBehavior: Returns a cited answer from your own IT documentation. This is the kind of question almost every company's onboarding content covers, so it works without seeding anything.
Returns a cited answer respecting the asker's permissions — the same question from two people with different access should not return content either of them can't see.

demoQueries.query: Ask about a step your docs don't cover
demoQueries.expectedBehavior: The hub says it has nothing on that and offers the escalation affordance, rather than inventing a plausible-sounding onboarding step.

steps.title: Pick a path
steps.description: Path A (Web SDK) renders Glean's chat UI via renderChat — fastest for a portal page with SSO. Path B (Platform Chat) calls POST /api/chat from your backend — you own every pixel and parse OpenAI Responses-style output with citation annotations.

aiPrompt:
Build an Onboarding Hub on Glean following
https://developers.glean.com/cookbook/onboarding-hub

1. Ask me which path: (A) Web SDK or (B) Platform Chat. Build the one
   I pick.
2. Build the checklist from MY onboarding content, not a fixed list:
   retrieve the onboarding docs my instance has and derive the steps
   from them. Ask me if you can't find any. Do not hardcode a named
   new hire or a step count.
3. Completion state in localStorage, with a progress ring and
   milestone badges grouped by the categories my own docs suggest.
4. Each step gets an "Ask about this" button that seeds a contextual
   question about that step.
5. Path A: renderChat in a sized #chat container (SSO cookie, no
   credential handling). Re-mount with initialMessage when "Ask about
   this" is clicked.
6. Path B: server-side POST /api/chat with { input, stream: false,
   store: true } and X_GLEAN_INCLUDE_EXPERIMENTAL=true. Parse
   output[0].content[0].text plus annotations[].sources[] for
   citations — NOT Client API chat.create fragment parsing. The token
   stays server-side.
7. When an answer comes back empty or uncited, show the escalation
   affordance (an IT or HR channel) instead of rendering nothing, and
   never let the model answer an onboarding question from its own
   knowledge. A new hire cannot tell an invented process from a real
   one, which makes fabrication the most damaging failure here.
8. Style it per the house style below: the real Glean logomark, Glean
   Blue (#343ced) as the accent.
9. Verify with the demo queries against my own content.
llmContext: Platform Chat (Path B): POST /api/chat, OpenAI Responses-style. Request: { input: string, stream?: boolean, store?: boolean }. Response: output[].content[].text + annotations[].sources[] (document/person/file/custom_entity). Experimental — requires X_GLEAN_INCLUDE_EXPERIMENTAL=true and backend platform.apiMigratedEndpointsEnabled. Platform scope is CHAT_WRITE (registry uses cookbook-style CHAT). No scoping/inclusion filter fields in OpenAPI — soft-scope via corpus framing only. Until @gleanwork/api-client ships glean.chat.create, use fetch against /api/chat. Path A: Web SDK renderChat with SSO cookie; all ChatOptions fields optional. Do NOT teach Client API glean.client.chat.create or messageType === 'CONTENT' fragment parsing in this recipe. The checklist and its steps must be derived from the reader's own onboarding content. An earlier draft seeded a named new hire's nine steps from a demo corpus that no longer exists, which made the hub display one fictional person's checklist on every instance. Ask rather than invent, and treat an empty or uncited answer as a state to render -- a new hire cannot distinguish an invented process from a real one.
